q: What law governs compensation for land acquired for midstream and downstream petroleum operations?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The compensation for land acquired for midstream and downstream petroleum operations is governed by the **Land Use Act**, as required by Section 115 of the Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, which mandates compliance with the provisions of the Land Use Act for such compensation【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 115】.

q: Name one ground on which a licence or permit may be revoked under Section 120.
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: One ground for revocation is that the holder becomes insolvent, bankrupt, enters into an agreement or composition with its creditors, or goes into liquidation (Section 120(a))【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 120】.

q: Name one offence under Section 230 relating to information given to the Commission or Authority.
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: One offence under Section 230 is furnishing a false or incomplete return to the Commission or Authority (paragraph (b))【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 230】.

q: How is the value of blended crude oil, condensates, or natural gas liquids determined?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The value of crude oil, condensates or natural gas liquids that have been blended is taken as the value at the measurement points where the streams are metered, and then adjusted for transport costs incurred within Nigeria. Before blending, each component must be measured by the lessee to determine its volume, quality and value. [Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 28 (1)–(2)]

q: What may a lessee do if insufficient natural gas is produced in a PML for production or injection needs?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: If the PML does not produce enough natural gas for production or injection, the lessee is permitted either to purchase the needed natural gas or to transfer natural gas from another PML for that purpose【Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 10】.

q: How does Regulation 47 define 'arm's length'?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: Regulation 47 of the Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022 provides that “arm’s length” means the relationship that exists between two or more persons, where none of such persons exerts or is in a position to exert significant influence on any of the other persons having regard to all relevant factors【Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 47】.

q: How often must a producer of gas submit its daily flaring and venting log to the Commission?
expected: Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 20
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: A producer of gas must submit its daily flaring and venting log to the Commission on a **monthly basis**, with the log to be filed **within 21 days after the end of each month**【Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 20】.

q: What is the administrative penalty for a licensee who fails to submit a decommissioning and abandonment plan on time?
expected: Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 24
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer: The Regulations provide that a licensee or lessee who does not submit a decommissioning and abandonment plan within the prescribed time is liable to an administrative penalty of **US $500,000 for each year of non‑compliance**, payable to the Commission (or the licence/lease may be revoked)【Regulation 24(1)】.

q: What must NNPC Limited's Board do if its external auditor cannot confirm the financial statements fairly represent the company?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: If the external auditor is unable to provide the required assurance that the financial statements fairly represent NNPC Limited, the Board must **immediately convene an extraordinary general meeting of the company**, **notify the shareholders**, and **consider any action that may be necessary** in that regard【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 62】.

q: What is the maximum duration of a petroleum prospecting licence for deep offshore acreage, and how is it split?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Act provides that a petroleum prospecting licence for deep offshore (and frontier) acreage may be granted for **a maximum of 10 years**, which is **divided into an initial exploration period of five years and an optional extension period of five years**【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 77】.

q: Who gives the Board of Trustees the matrix for sharing the trust fund among host communities?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The matrix for sharing the trust fund among host communities is provided to the Board of Trustees by the **settlor**【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 245】.

q: What must the Board of Trustees do with the reserve fund as it accrues?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Board of Trustees must **engage a fund manager to invest the reserve fund as the fund accrues** and must **manage the interest and profits from that investment, allocating the gains in accordance with section 244** of the Act【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 246】.

q: What hydrocarbon tax percentage applies to crude oil profits for onshore and shallow water prospecting licences selected on conversion?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The hydrocarbon tax rate for crude oil profits on onshore and shallow‑water petroleum prospecting licences that are selected on conversion (under section 93(6)(a) and (7)(a)) is **15 %** of the profit【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 267】.

q: If a petroleum company transfers a substantial part of its assets to avoid tax, who can the unpaid tax be recovered from?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: If a petroleum company transfers a substantial part of its assets to avoid paying income tax or hydrocarbon tax, the unpaid tax may be sued for and recovered from the person to whom the assets were transferred, i.e., the transferee, in the same way as any other tax recovery under section 294 of the Act【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 275】.

q: How is production allocated for a field straddling several mining leases under a unitization agreement, for royalty purposes?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: Under a unitization agreement, the allocation of production from a field that spans two or more petroleum mining leases (PMLs) must be specified in the unitization agreement itself. Each lessee is then responsible for paying royalty on the volume of production that has been allocated to them, unless the agreement provides an alternative methodology that has been approved by the Commission【Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 9】.

q: Who takes on decommissioning liability when an interest in a licence or lease is assigned?
expected: Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 23
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer: When an interest in a licence or lease is assigned (or otherwise transferred), the de‑commissioning and abandonment liability passes to the transferee.  Regulation 23 provides that the “proportionate liability … shall be deemed to be attached to the property transferred to the transferee” (B 1340).  Likewise, Regulation 17 states that for an assignment “the obligation shall be on the assignee to the extent that the assignee has assumed obligations” (17‑(1)(d)).  Thus, the assignee (or transferee) assumes the de‑commissioning liability, proportionate to the interest acquired and to the extent they have taken on the obligations.
